title: From three mandates (v0.1) to two mandate types, open or closed (v0.2)
caption: v0.1 chained an Intent Mandate, a merchant-signed Cart Mandate and a Payment Mandate. v0.2 removed Intent and Cart: a natural-language intent became machine-checkable constraints, and the cart became a merchant-signed checkout_jwt. Tutorials written in 2025 describe the v0.1 model.
alt: Flowchart in two parts. The v0.1 part shows IntentMandate with natural_language_description, merchants, skus, requires_refundability and intent_expiry, leading to CartMandate with CartContents, a W3C PaymentRequest and a merchant_authorization JWT carrying cart_hash, leading to PaymentMandate with payment_mandate_contents and user_authorization. The v0.2 part shows Open Checkout Mandate (mandate.checkout.open.1, constraints and cnf) and Open Payment Mandate (mandate.payment.open.1) linked by payment.reference, each extended by sd_hash into Closed Checkout Mandate (mandate.checkout.1 with checkout_jwt and checkout_hash) and Closed Payment Mandate (mandate.payment.1 with transaction_id, payee, payment_amount), which are linked because transaction_id equals checkout_hash. Dotted arrows show that IntentMandate was replaced by constraints, CartMandate by the merchant-signed checkout_jwt, and the v0.1 PaymentMandate split into closed and open forms.
